title: A closer look at whole grains
excerpt: Discover a little more color, texture, and variety in your next slice.
introduction: Whole-grain breads offer a wide range of experiences, from soft sandwich slices to robust country loaves. The name alone does not tell you how a bread will taste. A closer look at the flour blend and toppings helps you find the style you enjoy.
imageAlt: A whole-grain loaf topped with seeds
author: Crumb & Oven editorial team

sections.heading: Read beyond the color
sections.text: A dark loaf is not a complete description of its ingredients. Check the ingredient information or ask the bakery which grains are used. Blends can vary, and seeds on the outside tell a different story from the flour inside the dough. Clear information makes choosing easier.

sections.heading: Try a simple pairing first
sections.text: Taste a slice with something familiar, such as butter or your usual sandwich filling. Then try it toasted and notice the difference in aroma and texture. Starting with a simple pairing makes it easier to decide which qualities you want in your everyday bread.

sections.heading: Keep preferences in the conversation
sections.text: If you have ingredient restrictions, consult the bakery’s current ingredient and allergen information before choosing. A product name or photograph is not enough to confirm suitability. For flavor preferences, describe whether you like a softer slice, a hearty bite, or a seed-studded crust.
